text:
maria: Heads-up — after last night's batching/orchestration tweak (-enable-prefetch-priming=true) we're seeing KV prefix cache priming fail on several us-west pods. Hit-rate collapsed from ~82% to ~4% on affected hosts; 99th latency +220ms. Anyone else seeing this?

samir: yikes. which deploy? commit/hash?

maria: deploy-bot rolled canary at 2026-03-17T23:40 (sha a1b2c3f). The change was in autoscaler/batcher: grouping windows + moved prefetch/priming later in the pipeline. Thinking rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for canary (sha a1b2c3f) -> target rollback id rb-176123. Will post status.

max: I'm on it. Looking at perf and kv metrics now — miss rate spike lines up exactly with the rollout window. Preliminary: prefetch tasks are being queued after batch assembly which looks like they miss the window to prime other concurrent requests. Quick snippet from metrics:```
prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.041 (canary) vs 0.817 (previous)
prefetch_queue_len: spike from 5 -> 420
kv_worker_wait_us: median 1200 -> 7200
```

maria: can you paste the perf command / tail output you used? also curious if kernel selection changed (we saw some int8->fallback thrash earlier this month).

max: pasted the commands below — results trimmed for clarity.```
# perf capture on pod-03
$ sudo perf top -p $(pgrep runtime) --sort comm
# hot functions show: kv_lookup, prefetch_worker_loop, batch_assemble
# kernel path: int8_opt_kernel fallback_count=137 -> generic_kernel_count=137
# sequence shapes: avg_seq_len increased 12% due to extra misses
```
My read: the reordering made prefetch workers run after assembly so keys that would have been primed ahead are inserted too late; this causes a short-term eviction spiral when a noisy tenant bursts. That also increases variance, triggering less optimal kernel selection for a subset of batches.

samir: @infra-oncall can you check noisy-tenant churn? I see one tenant with a sudden traffic spike around the same time.

infra-oncall: confirmed — tenant "promo-canonical" had an experiment leak around 23:38 -> sustained ~3x baseline for 7m. They use very long prefixes which bloat the prefix space. That plus the reordering explains eviction pressure. No host-level OOMs, but cache churn is high.

aland: two quick mitigations: (1) rollback canary (already started) to restore prefetch-before-assembly ordering; (2) temporary tenant-affinity throttle for promo-canonical + pin prefetch workers to isolated cores to avoid starvation. I'll open PR for throttles now.

maria: :thumbsup: please also run a synthetic priming canary after rollback to validate. Add a short postmortem note in the incident ticket.

perf-bot: Alert cleared on canary after rollback. 1h moving avg prefix hit-rate back to 78% on canary group. 95th latency returned to baseline.

max: TL;DR root cause: ordering regression — prefetch moved after batch finalization. Consequences: missed priming windows -> cache cold inserts + eviction spiral when noisy-tenant burst overlapped -> increased misses caused longer sequences for some batches -> kernel selection fallback thrash and latency spikes.

samir: action items: add unit test that simulates prefetch-order inversion in CI, add load test with high-cardinality long-prefix traffic, add metric for prefetch_latency_vs_batch_assembly_latency, and add an automated canary that runs a small priming workload during rollout.

maria: opened incident IN-2026-319 and PR #4523 (rollback + throttle + tests). I'll draft a brief for all-hands. Thanks everyone.

max: post-incident note: also check our eviction policy — we should consider a small overprovision of prefix cache for experiments/rollouts or a soft-reserve for high-cardinality tenants to avoid cascade eviction on rollouts.

infra-oncall: no more anomalies in us-west after fixes. Closing monitoring loop once PRs land and canary stays green for 2h.

maria: OK closing thread — will add postmortem writeup later.
